mcq.q: The vine stores carbohydrates in its trunk and roots mainly to
choices: A Flavour the wine directly with starch
B Survive winter and fuel budburst before the new leaves photosynthesise
C Replace the need for water
mcq.answer: B Survive winter and fuel budburst before the new leaves photosynthesise
mcq.why: A weak, overcropped vine has poor reserves and a shaky start next spring.

mcq.q: Rain at harvest is a quality risk because it
choices: A Always improves noble rot in every region
B Swells berries (dilution), splits skins and encourages rot
C Raises tannin quality in every red
D Stops all machine harvesting by law
mcq.answer: B Swells berries (dilution), splits skins and encourages rot
mcq.why: The classic maritime and autumn-continental hazard; sorting becomes essential.

mcq.q: Birds and mammals are managed in vineyards by
choices: B Netting, bird of prey, shooting where legal, and fences — not by changing clone
mcq.answer: B Netting, bird of prey, shooting where legal, and fences — not by changing clone
mcq.why: Physical pests at ripeness; nets are common on small, valuable blocks.

mcq.q: A cover crop in a dry climate must be managed carefully because it can
choices: A Always add water to the vine
B Compete too hard for water and stop ripening
mcq.answer: B Compete too hard for water and stop ripening
mcq.why: The same tool that tames vigour in the Médoc can stress a dry-farmed bush vine.

mcq.q: A hyper-reductive Sauvignon ferment plus copper or aeration later might be used because
choices: B Strong reduction protects thiols in ferment but can leave sulphide notes that need careful treatment
C The wine is a red Port
mcq.answer: B Strong reduction protects thiols in ferment but can leave sulphide notes that need careful treatment
mcq.why: A style trade-off: maximum fruit versus cleanliness.

mcq.q: Co-inoculation of yeast and MLF bacteria is chosen to
choices: B Get MLF finished sooner, useful in cool cellars or for early bottling
D Replace SO2 at bottling entirely
mcq.answer: B Get MLF finished sooner, useful in cool cellars or for early bottling
mcq.why: Sequential MLF after the alcoholic ferment is the older, more controllable path.

mcq.q: A pneumatic press is valued for quality whites because it
choices: A Always gives the harshest press wine
B Allows a gentle, programmable squeeze and a clean fractioning of juice
C Replaces the need to sort fruit
mcq.answer: B Allows a gentle, programmable squeeze and a clean fractioning of juice
mcq.why: Whole-bunch Champagne presses and pneumatic tank presses are the gentle tools.

mcq.q: Blending before bottling is used to
choices: A Break the law in every PDO
B Balance variety, vineyard, barrel and vintage components into a consistent or complete wine
mcq.answer: B Balance variety, vineyard, barrel and vintage components into a consistent or complete wine
mcq.why: Bordeaux, Champagne NV and many New World labels are blending cultures.

mcq.q: Barsac, unlike most of Sauternes, may also label as
choices: B Sauternes (Barsac producers may use either name)
mcq.answer: B Sauternes (Barsac producers may use either name)
mcq.why: The Ciron still makes the mist; Barsac is often a little lighter in house style.

mcq.q: Canon-Fronsac, compared with generic Fronsac, is
choices: B A smaller, often better-sited limestone-clay zone for Merlot-led reds
mcq.answer: B A smaller, often better-sited limestone-clay zone for Merlot-led reds
mcq.why: A Right Bank value conversation next to Pomerol.

mcq.q: Fixin and Marsannay sit at the northern end of the Côte de Nuits and are known for
choices: B Relatively sturdy, earlier-priced Pinot (Marsannay also makes rosé and white)
mcq.answer: B Relatively sturdy, earlier-priced Pinot (Marsannay also makes rosé and white)
mcq.why: Marsannay is the only Côte d’Or village AOC that includes rosé in the village name story.

mcq.q: Givry is a Côte Chalonnaise AOC mainly for
choices: B Pinot Noir (and some Chardonnay), often a quality red source in the Chalonnaise
mcq.answer: B Pinot Noir (and some Chardonnay), often a quality red source in the Chalonnaise
mcq.why: Mercurey and Givry are the red addresses; Rully and Montagny lean white.

mcq.q: Bonnezeaux is
choices: B A sweet Chenin AOC on the Layon, with grand cru status
mcq.answer: B A sweet Chenin AOC on the Layon, with grand cru status
mcq.why: With Quarts de Chaume, the Layon’s historic sweet grands crus.

mcq.q: Saint-Nicolas-de-Bourgueil, compared with Bourgueil, is often
choices: B Slightly lighter, sandier Cabernet Franc
mcq.answer: B Slightly lighter, sandier Cabernet Franc
mcq.why: Same grape, a little more sand and early charm in many wines.

mcq.q: Condrieu’s typical style is
choices: A Bone-dry, light, high-acid like Muscadet
B Full, low-acid, apricot and blossom Viognier, usually dry, not for long cellaring in most cases
mcq.answer: B Full, low-acid, apricot and blossom Viognier, usually dry, not for long cellaring in most cases
mcq.why: Small AOC, ripe but not late-harvest; oak varies by producer.

mcq.q: Côtes du Rhône-Villages with a named commune (for example Séguret) sits
choices: A Above generic Côtes du Rhône and below the crus in the quality idea
mcq.answer: A Above generic Côtes du Rhône and below the crus in the quality idea
mcq.why: Learn the ladder; named villages have tighter rules than generic CdR.

mcq.q: Minervois La Livinière is
choices: B A cru of Minervois for more concentrated Mediterranean reds
mcq.answer: B A cru of Minervois for more concentrated Mediterranean reds
mcq.why: Languedoc’s named quality nest inside a larger AOC — a common local pattern (also Saint-Chinian Berlou/Roquebrun).

mcq.q: Alsace Muscat as a still wine is typically
choices: A A sweet SGN by default
B Dry, grapey and floral, used as an aperitif
mcq.answer: B Dry, grapey and floral, used as an aperitif
mcq.why: Two Muscats are used; the dry still style is the exam default unless VT/SGN is stated.

mcq.q: Barbera d’Alba, next to the Barolo zone, is typically
choices: A Paler and more tannic than Barolo
B A juicy, high-acid everyday red from Barbera, not Nebbiolo
mcq.answer: B A juicy, high-acid everyday red from Barbera, not Nebbiolo
mcq.why: Alba vs Asti is a zone distinction; the grape is the same family.

mcq.q: Carmignano DOCG is notable in Tuscany because it
choices: B Historically allowed Cabernet with Sangiovese, foreshadowing Super Tuscans
mcq.answer: B Historically allowed Cabernet with Sangiovese, foreshadowing Super Tuscans
mcq.why: A small, older DOC story west of Florence.

mcq.q: Valpolicella Valpantena is
choices: B A defined valley mention within Valpolicella, not a drying method
mcq.answer: B A defined valley mention within Valpolicella, not a drying method
mcq.why: Geography (Classico, Valpantena) versus method (Ripasso, Amarone).

mcq.q: Carricante on Etna, compared with lowland Nero d’Avola, gives wines that are
choices: A Riper, lower in acid and darker
B Whiter, higher in acid, more herbal-citrus, from altitude and volcanic soils
mcq.answer: B Whiter, higher in acid, more herbal-citrus, from altitude and volcanic soils
mcq.why: Do not sit Etna and Vittoria in the same climate box.

mcq.q: Campo de Borja’s old Garnacha vines tend to give
choices: B Ripe, spicy, good-value reds from a continental Aragón site
mcq.answer: B Ripe, spicy, good-value reds from a continental Aragón site
mcq.why: The ‘Empire of Garnacha’ marketing line is based on real old vineyards.

mcq.q: Monterrei and Ribeira Sacra are Galician DOs that, unlike Rías Baixas, also emphasise
choices: B Mencía reds (especially Ribeira Sacra’s terraces) as well as local whites
mcq.answer: B Mencía reds (especially Ribeira Sacra’s terraces) as well as local whites
mcq.why: Ribeira Sacra’s Sil/Miño canyons are among Spain’s most dramatic vineyards.

mcq.q: A modern, unoaked Rioja Tinto Joven is likely to taste of
choices: A Coconut, brick and leather only
B Primary red/black fruit with little developed oak
D Banana carbonic only by law
mcq.answer: B Primary red/black fruit with little developed oak
mcq.why: Not all Rioja is Reserva; joven is the fruit-first end of the same grape.

mcq.q: Rheingau Rüdesheim or Hochheim Riesling, compared with a light Mosel Kabinett, is often
choices: A Even lower in alcohol and always sparkling
B A little fuller and more powerful, from a warmer, broader Rhine slope
C A red Spätburgunder by law
mcq.answer: B A little fuller and more powerful, from a warmer, broader Rhine slope
mcq.why: The Rhine’s east–west stretch is a heat trap relative to the Mosel twists.

mcq.q: Santorini Assyrtiko that has seen oak or long lees, compared with a stainless village wine, will show more
choices: B Texture and a less purely citrus profile, while acid should remain high
mcq.answer: B Texture and a less purely citrus profile, while acid should remain high
mcq.why: Nykteri is the traditional late-picked, often oak-aged style.

mcq.q: Vinho Regional Alentejano compared with DOC Alentejo is
choices: A Always higher quality by law
B The PGI tier, more flexible on varieties, sitting beside the DOC
mcq.answer: B The PGI tier, more flexible on varieties, sitting beside the DOC
mcq.why: Same landscape, two legal boxes — like IGP Pays d’Oc beside Languedoc AOC.

mcq.q: Bairrada white wines of quality are often based on
choices: B Bical and Maria Gomes (Fernão Pires), high in acid, sometimes sparkling too
mcq.answer: B Bical and Maria Gomes (Fernão Pires), high in acid, sometimes sparkling too
mcq.why: The region is not only Baga; traditional-method fizz is a local extra.

mcq.q: Stags Leap District and Howell Mountain are Napa AVAs that differ mainly in
choices: A Grape: only Pinot is allowed on Howell
B Mesoclimate and soil: valley-floor/bench Cabernet versus higher, cooler mountain Cabernet
mcq.answer: B Mesoclimate and soil: valley-floor/bench Cabernet versus higher, cooler mountain Cabernet
mcq.why: Mountain AVAs (Howell, Diamond, Spring, Mount Veeder, Atlas Peak) are a Napa revision theme.

mcq.q: Maule and Itata in southern Chile are associated with
choices: A Only new, irrigated Cabernet on fertile flats
B Older dry-farmed País and Muscat, plus a revival of bush-vine reds and coastal Cinsault
mcq.answer: B Older dry-farmed País and Muscat, plus a revival of bush-vine reds and coastal Cinsault
mcq.why: The historic south, not the Maipo brochure.

mcq.q: Eden Valley, above Barossa, is cooler and is prized for
choices: A The ripest fortified Muscat in Australia
B Riesling and a more restrained Shiraz than the valley floor
mcq.answer: B Riesling and a more restrained Shiraz than the valley floor
mcq.why: A paired revision fact with Clare: South Australia’s Riesling pair.

mcq.q: Central Otago Pinot Noir, compared with Marlborough Pinot, is typically
choices: A Lighter, greener and always sparkling
B Riper and more structured, from a continental inland climate
mcq.answer: B Riper and more structured, from a continental inland climate
mcq.why: Marlborough can make good Pinot, but Otago is the specialist region.

mcq.q: A PDO wine in the EU must have
choices: A No link to a place
B Grapes from the defined area and production to the registered specification
C Only a vintage, never a place
mcq.answer: B Grapes from the defined area and production to the registered specification
mcq.why: PDO vs PGI vs wine without GI is core LO law.

mcq.q: Brunello di Montalcino Riserva, compared with the normale, requires
choices: B A longer minimum ageing before release
mcq.answer: B A longer minimum ageing before release
mcq.why: Time is the extra legal hoop; the grape stays Sangiovese.

mcq.q: Variety claims on an Australian still-wine label usually require
mcq.answer: B 85% of that variety
mcq.why: 85% for variety, vintage and GI is the standard Australian trio.

mcq.q: The taille in Champagne is
choices: B A later press fraction, more phenolic, used with care or not at all in top wines
mcq.answer: B A later press fraction, more phenolic, used with care or not at all in top wines
mcq.why: Cuvée versus taille is a quality sorting at the press.

mcq.q: A house that blocks MLF in its Champagne base wines is usually seeking
choices: B A tighter, higher-acid style that may need time or dosage to balance
mcq.answer: B A tighter, higher-acid style that may need time or dosage to balance
mcq.why: MLF is a house-style fork, not a legal requirement.

mcq.q: Prosecco DOC from the plains, compared with Conegliano-Valdobbiadene DOCG, is typically
choices: A Always traditional method and drier
B Higher volume, simpler, and more often from higher-yielding sites
mcq.answer: B Higher volume, simpler, and more often from higher-yielding sites
mcq.why: Hills, yields and price are the quality story, not a different grape.

mcq.q: New Zealand traditional-method wines are most convincing from
choices: A The hottest Gisborne flats only
B Cooler sites (for example parts of Marlborough, Central Otago or a specialist estate) with Champagne grapes
mcq.answer: B Cooler sites (for example parts of Marlborough, Central Otago or a specialist estate) with Champagne grapes
mcq.why: Method and cool fruit matter more than the national Sauvignon brand.

mcq.q: If a sparkling wine is labelled Extra Brut it may contain
mcq.answer: B 0–6 g/L sugar
mcq.why: Drier than Brut; not as absolute as Brut Nature’s no-added-sugar idea.

mcq.q: A Fino and an Oloroso started from similar Palomino wines; the fork is
choices: B Fortification strength and whether flor is encouraged or prevented
C The colour of the bottle
mcq.answer: B Fortification strength and whether flor is encouraged or prevented
mcq.why: About 15% and flor versus about 17% and no flor is the teaching model.

mcq.q: Tawny Port with an age indication (10, 20, 30, 40) is
choices: B A blend whose average character matches that age, aged oxidatively in wood
mcq.answer: B A blend whose average character matches that age, aged oxidatively in wood
mcq.why: Not a legal average of every litre to the month; it is a style claim tasted by the IVDP.

mcq.q: Sercial Madeira’s high acid means that even when labelled dry it can
choices: A Taste flabby and low in flavour
B Taste almost austere in youth and age for decades
mcq.answer: B Taste almost austere in youth and age for decades
mcq.why: Acid is Madeira’s preservative with heat and spirit.

mcq.q: Muscat de Beaumes-de-Venise should be drunk
choices: A After twenty years in a hot garage
B Young and chilled, while the grape aroma is still primary
C Decanted for crust like old Vintage Port
mcq.answer: B Young and chilled, while the grape aroma is still primary
mcq.why: A youthful VDN; not a Rutherglen Rare.

mcq.q: Pedro Ximénez from Montilla-Moriles is often
choices: A A pale biological Fino only
B Unfortified or lightly fortified because the dried grapes are already extremely sweet
mcq.answer: B Unfortified or lightly fortified because the dried grapes are already extremely sweet
mcq.why: Heat and asoleo do the concentration; some wines need little spirit.

mcq.q: A wine that is ‘fully developed’ on the SAT is
choices: B At a mature flavour stage, which may still be pleasant for some years
mcq.answer: B At a mature flavour stage, which may still be pleasant for some years
mcq.why: Fully developed is not the same as tired.

mcq.q: The first thing to check when a guest says a wine is ‘off’ is whether
choices: A You should argue about price
B The fault is in the glass (detergent, leftover red) or in the bottle (TCA, oxidation, VA)
mcq.answer: B The fault is in the glass (detergent, leftover red) or in the bottle (TCA, oxidation, VA)
mcq.why: Pour a fresh glass; then open a second bottle if TCA is suspected.

mcq.q: A salty, fried tapas plate is most comfortable with a wine that has
choices: A High tannin, high alcohol and residual bitterness
B High acid and/or bubbles, and not too much oak or tannin
C No fruit and a warm service temperature
mcq.answer: B High acid and/or bubbles, and not too much oak or tannin
mcq.why: Salt loves acid; fry loves bubbles; tannin and heat do not love salt the same way.

mcq.q: Ideal humidity in a long-term cork cellar is roughly
choices: A Bone dry, to protect labels only
B About 60–80%, enough to keep corks from shrinking
C A swimming-pool fog that soaks every case
mcq.answer: B About 60–80%, enough to keep corks from shrinking
mcq.why: Too dry: corks shrink; too wet: labels and cartons suffer, wine inside is usually fine.

written.title: Question 1 — Burgundy hierarchy and Côte d’Or reds

parts.prompt: Set out the Burgundy quality ladder from regional wine to Grand Cru, and state what legally changes as you climb.
points: Regional (Bourgogne, sometimes with a modifier) → village → Premier Cru (named climat) → Grand Cru (the climat is the AOC).
Smaller area, lower maximum yield, tighter place name, usually higher price and ageing potential.
Grape remains Pinot Noir (reds) or Chardonnay (whites) in the Côte d’Or story.
A Premier Cru is a village AOC plus a climat; a Grand Cru is its own AOC.
Côte de Nuits vs Côte de Beaune as the village map.
Do not invent a Grand Cru.

parts.prompt: Why do Gevrey-Chambertin, Vosne-Romanée and Volnay produce different Pinot styles if the grape is the same?
points: Site: aspect, slope position, limestone vs more clay, drainage.
Mesoclimate: Nuits slightly cooler/firmer stereotype vs Beaune; village folklore (Gevrey sturdy, Vosne spicy/velvet, Volnay fragrant).
Producer: whole bunch, extraction, new oak, stem ripeness.
Clone and vine age.
Yield and sorting in a wet year.
You must link at least one named village to a style without inventing AOCs.

parts.prompt: Describe typical red winemaking for a village Côte de Nuits Pinot intended to age.
points: Hand harvest, sort, destem or include ripe whole bunches, cold soak optional.
Gentle extraction (pigéage), not a 30-day pump-over as if it were Cabernet.
MLF, 12–18 months in a modest share of new oak (228 L), rack, bottle.
Avoid over-oak and over-extraction of green stems.
SO2 after MLF; no chaptalisation needed in a ripe year (allowed in cool years where law permits).
State the style: pale to medium colour, highish acid, fine tannin, red fruit to spice.

parts.prompt: Explain Marlborough’s climate and why Sauvignon Blanc from Wairau and Awatere can differ.
points: Cool, sunny, dry by NZ standards, large diurnal range; mountains and sea.
Wairau: riper passion fruit/citrus in many wines.
Awatere: cooler, windier, more green herb/grapefruit.
Stony soils, irrigation often needed.
Machine harvest at night is common for volume.
Vintage rain still happens.

parts.prompt: Place Central Otago, Hawke’s Bay and Martinborough on the map with a grape and a climate note each.
points: Central Otago: South Island inland, continental, Pinot Noir, ripe structure.
Hawke’s Bay: North Island east, warmer, Bordeaux blends and Syrah on Gimblett Gravels; also Chardonnay.
Martinborough / Wairarapa: south-east North Island, cool, windy, low-yield Pinot.
Do not put Gimblett Gravels in Otago.
Gisborne as a Chardonnay extra can score.
All are still-wine stories here, not Méthode Marlborough unless clearly extra.

parts.prompt: Outline the standard winery recipe for high-volume Marlborough Sauvignon and one change a premium single-vineyard wine might make.
points: Volume: machine, night, reductive, cultured yeast, cool stainless, no MLF, no oak, early bottle, screwcap.
Premium: hand or better fruit, some lees, a little old oak or amphora, wild yeast, later pick or extra hang-time, lower yield, maybe a splash of barrel ferment.
Both keep thiols and acid in front if they are still Sauvignon.
A change that would hide the variety (heavy new oak, MLF butter) is usually a fault of judgement, not a plus.
State the style contrast: pungent and simple vs more texture and site.

parts.prompt: Describe Prosecco production from grape to bottle, including how sweetness is set.
points: Glera, early-ish pick for acid, cool climate of the north-east.
Press, settle, first ferment to a dry or nearly dry base in tank.
Second ferment in pressurised tank (Charmat/Martinotti) with sugar and yeast.
Stop and filter; dosage/adjustment sets Brut through Dry/Extra Dry.
Bottle under pressure; drink young; no riddling.
Col Fondo / ancestral on lees as a minority style can score.

parts.prompt: Distinguish Prosecco DOC, Conegliano-Valdobbiadene DOCG, Rive and Cartizze.
points: DOC: large plains and foothills, volume.
Conegliano-Valdobbiadene Superiore DOCG: historic hills, tighter rules.
Rive: named village/vineyard hillsides, vintage-dated, lower yield.
Superiore di Cartizze: a small plot, riper, often a little richer/sweeter in practice.
Asolo DOCG as another hill zone can score.
Grape remains Glera.

parts.prompt: Why is Extra Dry a common Prosecco sweetness, and how should it be served with food?
points: Glera’s fruit sits well with a little sugar; Extra Dry (12–17 g/L) tastes off-dry, not ‘extra dry’.
Serve well chilled, young, as an aperitif or with lightly sweet/savoury canapés, prosciutto and melon.
A Brut version is better with salty fried food if you want a drier match.
Avoid a very sweet cake (needs Demi-sec or Moscato) and avoid tannic steak.
Do not cellar a basic DOC like vintage Champagne.

written.title: Question 4 — Fortified Muscat and cellar practice

parts.prompt: Compare Muscat de Beaumes-de-Venise with Rutherglen Muscat and with a dry Alsace Muscat.
points: Beaumes: VDN, mutage, youthful, grape/flower, pale, chilled, Southern Rhône heat.
Rutherglen: fortified, long oxidative wood, brown, raisin/tea/toffee, Grand/Rare tiers, north-east Victoria heat.
Alsace Muscat: unfortified, usually dry, grapey aperitif, cool-continental, variety-labelled still wine.
All share Muscat aroma compounds; process and climate change everything else.
Sweetness: Alsace dry (usually); the other two sweet.
Ageing: Alsace and Beaumes young; Rutherglen can be ancient.

parts.prompt: Give storage advice for an unopened bottle of each, and for an opened bottle.
points: Unopened Alsace: cool, dark, drink in a few years; not a 30-year cellar wine unless VT/SGN.
Unopened Beaumes: cool, dark, drink in a few years; fridge after opening, a few days.
Unopened Rutherglen: very stable; store like other oxidatives, upright is fine once for service; opened lasts weeks to months if cool.
Heat and light damage all three.
Do not store opened Beaumes in a warm bar for a month.
Cork vs screwcap does not beat heat.

parts.prompt: Pair each wine with food, with one reason each.
points: Alsace Muscat: asparagus or lightly spiced aperitif food — aroma without sweetness clash.
Beaumes: fruit tart or blue cheese — sweetness match, floral lift.
Rutherglen: dark chocolate or Christmas pudding — density and oxidative notes.
Do not put dry Alsace Muscat on a pudding or Rutherglen on delicate oysters.
State service temperature in one clause each if not already credited.
